Survival phrases
Hello
Polite default greeting, any time of day.
A: 안녕하세요annyeonghaseyo, 처음cheoeum 뵙겠습니다boepgetseumnida.
B: 네ne, 안녕하세요annyeonghaseyo! 반갑습니다bangapseumnida.
Hello, nice to meet you for the first time. / Hi! Nice to meet you.

Survival phrases
Thank you
Formal. Casual: 고마워 (gomawo).
🗣 [감사함니다] 비음화
A: 도와주셔서dowajusyeoseo 감사합니다gamsahamnida.
B: 아니에요anieyo, 별말씀을요byeolmalsseumeullyo.
Thank you for helping. / Not at all.

Survival phrases
I'm sorry
Formal apology. 미안해 (mianhae) = casual.
🗣 [죄송함니다] 비음화
A: 늦어서neujeoseo 죄송합니다joesonghamnida.
B: 괜찮아요gwaenchanayo, 저도jeodo 방금banggeum 왔어요wasseoyo.
Sorry I'm late. / It's fine, I just got here too.

Survival phrases
How much is it?
Point at the item and ask.
A: 이거igeo 얼마예요eolmayeyo?
B: 만man 이천icheon 원이에요wonieyo.
How much is this? / 12,000 won.

Survival phrases
Where is the bathroom?
어디예요eodiyeyo = where is.
A: 저기요jeogiyo, 화장실hwajangsil 어디예요eodiyeyo?
B: 저쪽으로jeojjogeuro 쭉jjuk 가시면gasimyeon 돼요dwaeyo.
Excuse me, where's the bathroom? / Go straight that way.

Survival phrases
This one, please
Ordering or shopping. 주세요juseyo = please give.
A: 뭐mwo 드릴까요deurilkkayo?
B: 이거igeo 주세요juseyo. 포장이요pojangiyo.
What can I get you? / This one, to go.

Survival phrases
It's okay / I'm fine
Also used to politely refuse.
🗣 [괜차나요] ㅎ 탈락
A: 괜찮아요gwaenchanayo? 다쳤어요dachyeosseoyo?
B: 네ne, 괜찮아요gwaenchanayo.
Are you okay? Hurt? / Yes, I'm fine.

Survival phrases
Please speak slowly
Lifesaver phrase.
A: 죄송한데joesonghande 천천히cheoncheonhi 말해malhae 주세요juseyo.
B: 아a, 네ne. 천천히cheoncheonhi 할게요halgeyo.
Sorry, please speak slowly. / Ah, sure, I'll slow down.

Survival phrases
I don't speak Korean well
Buys you patience.
🗣 [한구거 잘 모태요] 연음, 격음화
A: 한국어hangugeo 잘하시네요jalhasineyo!
B: 아니에요anieyo, 아직ajik 잘jal 못해요motaeyo.
Your Korean is good! / No, I'm still not good.

Survival phrases
Just a moment / excuse me
Squeezing past someone on the subway.
🗣 [잠시마뇨] 연음
A: 잠시만요jamsimanyo, 지나갈게요jinagalgeyo.
B: 네ne, 가세요gaseyo.
Excuse me, coming through. / Go ahead.

Survival phrases 2
Excuse me (to get attention)
Call a waiter or stop a stranger. Not an apology.
A: 저기요jeogiyo! 메뉴판menyupan 좀jom 주세요juseyo.
B: 네ne, 잠시만요jamsimanyo.
Excuse me! The menu, please. / Yes, one moment.

Survival phrases 2
Please help me
Emergency or just a heavy bag.
A: 저기요jeogiyo, 좀jom 도와주세요dowajuseyo.
B: 네ne, 뭐가mwoga 필요하세요piryohaseyo?
Excuse me, please help me. / Sure, what do you need?

Survival phrases 2
Please say it again
다시dasi = again.
A: 죄송한데joesonghande 다시dasi 말해malhae 주세요juseyo.
B: 지하철역은jihacheollyeogeun 왼쪽이에요oenjjogieyo.
Sorry, say that again please. / The subway station is on the left.

Survival phrases 2
Can you speak English?
할hal 수su 있다itda = can do.
🗣 [영어 할 수 이써요] 연음
A: 영어yeongeo 할hal 수su 있어요isseoyo?
B: 조금요jogeumyo. 천천히cheoncheonhi 말할게요malhalgeyo.
Can you speak English? / A little. I'll speak slowly.

Survival phrases 2
What is this?
Point and ask. Works for food, signs, everything.
A: 이게ige 뭐예요mwoyeyo?
B: 떡볶이예요tteokbokkiyeyo. 조금jogeum 매워요maewoyo.
What is this? / Tteokbokki. It's a bit spicy.

Survival phrases 2
Do you take cards?
돼요dwaeyo = is it possible / does it work.
A: 카드kadeu 돼요dwaeyo?
B: 네ne, 돼요dwaeyo. 여기yeogi 꽂아kkoja 주세요juseyo.
Do you take cards? / Yes. Insert it here.

Survival phrases 2
What's the wifi password?
비밀번호bimilbeonho = password.
A: 와이파이waipai 비밀번호가bimilbeonhoga 뭐예요mwoyeyo?
B: 영수증에yeongsujeunge 있어요isseoyo.
What's the wifi password? / It's on the receipt.

Survival phrases 2
I'm lost
길gil = road/way. 잃다ilta = to lose.
🗣 [기를 이러써요] 연음, ㅎ 탈락
A: 길을gireul 잃었어요ireosseoyo. 여기가yeogiga 어디예요eodiyeyo?
B: 여기yeogi 홍대예요hongdaeyeyo. 어디eodi 가세요gaseyo?
I'm lost. Where is this? / This is Hongdae. Where are you going?

Asking around
Where is the bathroom?
Full form. Short: 화장실hwajangsil 어디예요eodiyeyo? Both fine.
🗣 [화장시리 어디에 이써요] 연음

Asking around
Could you take a photo for us?
Extra polite with 주실래요jusillaeyo. Hand over the phone after.
🗣 [사진 좀 찌거 주실래요] 연음
A: 혹시hoksi 사진sajin 좀jom 찍어jjigeo 주시겠어요jusigesseoyo?
B: 네ne, 그럼요geureomyo. 하나hana, 둘dul, 셋set!
Would you mind taking a photo? / Of course. One, two, three!

Introductions
I'm ___
Look at the last Hangul block: 이에요ieyo after a final consonant (저는jeoneun 킴이에요kimieyo), 예요yeyo after a vowel (저는jeoneun 리사예요risayeyo).

Introductions
What's your name?
Polite: 성함이seonghami 어떻게eotteoke 되세요doeseyo? for elders or formal settings.
🗣 [이르미 뭐예요] 연음
A: 이름이ireumi 뭐예요mwoyeyo?
B: 저는jeoneun 민수입니다minsuimnida. 이름이ireumi 뭐예요mwoyeyo?
What's your name? / I'm Minsu. What's yours?

Introductions
Nice to meet you
Lit. 'glad because we met'. Formal: 반갑습니다bangapseumnida.
A: 만나서mannaseo 반가워요bangawoyo.
B: 저도jeodo 반가워요bangawoyo.
Nice to meet you. / Nice to meet you too.

Introductions
Where are you from?
에서eseo = from. 어디eodi = where.
🗣 [어디에서 와써요] 연음
A: 어디에서eodieseo 왔어요wasseoyo?
B: 필리핀에서pillipineseo 왔어요wasseoyo. 세부요sebuyo.
Where are you from? / From the Philippines. Cebu.

Introductions
How old are you?
Normal question in Korea; it decides how people speak to each other.
🗣 [멷 사리에요] 받침 → ㄷ, 연음
A: 실례지만sillyejiman 나이가naiga 어떻게eotteoke 되세요doeseyo?
B: 스물여덟이요seumullyeodeolbiyo. 그쪽은요geujjogeunyo?
Excuse me, how old are you? / 28. And you?

Introductions
What do you do?
일il = work. 직업이jigeobi 뭐예요mwoyeyo? also works.
A: 무슨museun 일il 해요haeyo?
B: IT 회사에서hoesaeseo 일해요ilhaeyo.
What do you do? / I work at an IT company.

Introductions
I'm studying Korean
공부하다gongbuhada = to study. Say this and people light up.
🗣 [한구거 공부해요] 연음
A: 한국어hangugeo 공부해요gongbuhaeyo?
B: 네ne, 매일maeil 조금씩jogeumssik 해요haeyo.
Do you study Korean? / Yes, a little every day.

Introductions
What's your hobby?
취미chwimi = hobby. 제je 취미는chwimineun 운동이에요undongieyo = my hobby is working out.
A: 취미가chwimiga 뭐예요mwoyeyo?
B: 달리기하고dalligihago 음악이요eumagiyo.
What's your hobby? / Running and music.

Introductions
Please take care of me
Said after introducing yourself at work or in a group. No English equivalent.
🗣 [잘 부탁드림니다] 비음화
A: 오늘부터oneulbuteo 같이gachi 일하게ilhage 됐어요dwaesseoyo. 잘jal 부탁드립니다butakdeurimnida.
B: 네ne, 저도jeodo 잘jal 부탁드려요butakdeuryeoyo.
I'm starting work with you today. Please take care of me. / Likewise.

Small talk
How have you been?
Standard greeting for someone you haven't seen in a while.
🗣 [잘 지내써요] 연음
A: 오랜만이에요oraenmanieyo! 잘jal 지냈어요jinaesseoyo?
B: 네ne, 덕분에요deokbuneyo. 잘jal 지냈어요jinaesseoyo?

Small talk
How are things lately?
요즘yojeum = these days. 어때요eottaeyo = how is it.
A: 요즘yojeum 어때요eottaeyo?
B: 바빠요bappayo. 그래도geuraedo 재밌어요jaemisseoyo.
How are things lately? / Busy. But fun.

Small talk
So-so
Lit. 'it's just like that'. Very common honest answer.
A: 요즘yojeum 어때요eottaeyo?
B: 그냥geunyang 그래요geuraeyo. 바쁘기만bappeugiman 해요haeyo.
How are things? / So-so. Just busy.

Small talk
Nice weather, isn't it
네요neyo ending = noticing something out loud. 날씨가nalssiga 춥네요chumneyo = it's cold, huh.
🗣 [날씨가 존네요] 비음화, 받침 중화
A: 오늘oneul 날씨가nalssiga 좋네요jonneyo.
B: 네ne, 산책하기sanchaekagi 딱ttak 좋아요joayo.
Nice weather today. / Yes, perfect for a walk.

Small talk
What are you doing this weekend?
주말jumal = weekend, 에e = on.
🗣 [주마레 뭐 해요] 연음
A: 주말에jumare 뭐mwo 해요haeyo?
B: 등산deungsan 가요gayo. 같이gachi 갈래요gallaeyo?
What are you doing this weekend? / Going hiking. Want to come?

Small talk
Me too
Casual: 나도nado.
A: 저jeo 커피keopi 중독이에요jungdogieyo.
B: 저도요jeodoyo! 하루에harue 세se 잔은janeun 마셔요masyeoyo.
I'm a coffee addict. / Me too! At least three cups a day.

Small talk
Really?
Softer than 진짜요jinjjayo?. Both fine.
🗣 [정말료] ㄴ 첨가 → ㄹㄹ
A: 저jeo 다음daeum 달에dare 한국hanguk 가요gayo.
B: 정말요jeongmallyo? 어디로eodiro 가요gayo?
I'm going to Korea next month. / Really? Where to?

Small talk
See you again
또tto = again. 내일naeil 봐요bwayo = see you tomorrow.
A: 오늘oneul 재밌었어요jaemisseosseoyo. 또tto 봐요bwayo!
B: 네ne, 연락할게요yeollakalgeyo.
Today was fun. See you again! / Yes, I'll be in touch.

Goodbye (to someone leaving)
가세요gaseyo = go well. Say it when THEY are leaving.
A: 저jeo 먼저meonjeo 갈게요galgeyo. 안녕히annyeonghi 계세요gyeseyo.

Goodbye (to someone staying)
계세요gyeseyo = stay well. Say it when YOU are leaving.
A: 저jeo 이만iman 가ga 볼게요bolgeyo. 안녕히annyeonghi 계세요gyeseyo.
B: 네ne, 조심히josimhi 가세요gaseyo.
I should get going. Goodbye. / Okay, get home safe.
